step_reviews.reason: For each s>0, mu↦E logistic(mu+sZ-b1) is C1, strictly increasing with limits0 and1. Logistic derivative is bounded and strictlypositive, and E|Z|<infinity. Thus the implicit derivative is valid locally; uniqueness patches the local curves into one C1 curve for every finite s>0.

Write A=E fprime>0 and weight w=fprime*phi/A. Substitution of muprime=-E[Z fprime]/A gives dp2/ds=A Cov_w(Z,gprime/fprime). Independently computed d log[r(t)]/dt=2(d-1)/((d+t)(1+t))>0 for d>1,t>0; multiplying by r gives the stated derivative. Since dt/dZ=s*t>0 and weighted Z has a positive density, the independent-copy covariance identity is strictly positive. The ratio is bounded between1/d and d, ensuring integrability. Strict increase over the connected s>0 domain proves global injectivity of the two-marginal map, not merely local nonzeroJacobian.

Independent matrix-calculus calculation gives partial_K log phi=-tr(Sigma^-1 D)/2+x^T Sigma^-1 D Sigma^-1 x/2, with D offdiagonal ones. It equals phi_xy/phi, so no missing factor2 occurs. On compact |K|<T subdomains the density derivatives are polynomial times a uniformly Gaussian tail; bounded logistic factors/derivatives justify differentiation and both integrations byparts. Product logistic derivatives is everywherepositive, hence qprime(K)>0 and globalinjectivity.

At each of two moderatorlevels BOTH MZ andDZ conditional distributions must be observed. T and bothK then give A=2(KMZ-KDZ), C=2KDZ-KMZ, E=T-KMZ. Allpositive ACE imply0<KDZ<KMZ<T, inside the Gaussian derivative domain.

Two distinct moderatorlevels make the affine-design determinant nonzero. Taking logs of each positive recoveredvariance identifies its two coefficients, and the two recoveredmeans identify the mean intercept/slope. For continuous support, common conditional support and equality-a.e./continuity need explicit treatment; point conditioning at unsupported values is not valid.

Probability0/1, infinite means/variances/difficulties and zero variancecomponents are outside thefiniteinterior assumptions. Numerical saturation is not mathematical nonidentification.

Known unequal OPLM slopes are not covered. No claim of empiricalOPLM nonidentifiability follows.
